notes.meaning: God was near the end of his forty days of teaching Moses on the mountain. Now he names the man who will build the tabernacle, the holy tent for worship. To "call by name" means God chose and appointed Bezalel himself for this special work. Because God made the choice, no one had reason to argue over the job or envy the man chosen. Bezalel's name means "in the shadow of God." He was from Judah, and his grandfather Hur was probably the Hur who helped hold up Moses' hands in battle.

God filled Bezalel with his Spirit to give him wisdom, understanding, knowledge and skill in every kind of craft. The Israelites had been brick-makers in Egypt, not goldsmiths or jewelers, so God supplied the skill they lacked. The sources draw a warm lesson from this. Even ordinary skill with our hands is a gift from God's Spirit. It deserves respect, and God deserves the praise for it.

Bezalel's gifts covered every part of the work. He could plan artistic designs and work in gold, silver and bronze. He could also cut and set precious stones and carve wood. God had described everything in detail, but someone still had to work out the designs so the finished work matched God's plan.

God gave Bezalel a partner, Oholiab, from the tribe of Dan, one of the less honored tribes. In this way God honored a humbler part of his people, much as Paul says every part of the body is needed. God also put wisdom into all the skilled workers. Each one's gift was given so they could make what God commanded, not to serve their own ends. When our gifts grow, it is the Spirit's continued work in us.

God lists what the craftsmen are to make. The list includes the tent itself and the ark, the sacred chest that held God's law. It also includes the mercy seat, the gold lid on the ark, along with the table, the lampstand, the two altars and the washing basin on its stand. The careful list shows that God wanted the work done in order, with nothing forgotten. The lampstand is called "pure" because it was made of pure gold.

The workers were also to make the priests' clothing, both Aaron's holy garments and his sons' garments. They were to prepare the anointing oil, used to set apart the priests and the holy objects, and the sweet incense. Everything was to be made exactly as God had commanded. It followed the pattern God had shown Moses.

Right after the building plans, God reminds Israel to keep his Sabbaths, the weekly days of rest. The people might have thought such holy work was important enough to do even on the Sabbath, but even building the tabernacle had to stop for God's day of rest. The Sabbath was a sign of God's special favor that marked Israel out from other nations. It reminded them that the LORD "sanctifies" them, meaning he sets them apart as his own.

The Sabbath is "holy to you." That means it was given for the people's good as well as for God's honor. Anyone who broke it by working was to be put to death or "cut off" from the people. Here the two phrases seem to mean the same thing. Such a heavy penalty shows how seriously God took the Sabbath. Breaking it openly was a sign of contempt for the mark God had put on his people. Acts of worship and mercy were not counted as forbidden work.

People could work for six days, but the seventh was a Sabbath of complete rest, like a "high Sabbath." It was set apart from ordinary use for God. By keeping it, people learned to rest from worldly busyness and give themselves, and all they have, to God. The warning of death is repeated to show how much it mattered.

Israel was to keep the Sabbath in every generation as a lasting covenant, a binding agreement between God and his people. It was one of the most lasting signs of that covenant. The Sabbath also pointed ahead to the final rest God promises his people.

differ.view: Reformed teachers stress that the Sabbath's meaning lasts. Matthew Henry says its moral duty continues until the end of time. Calvin says its outward rules ended with Christ, but its true meaning remains.
Under the new covenant Christians are not bound by the Sabbath. The lasting lesson is that our work for God must never crowd out our rest in what Christ has already done for us.
Because this command is spoken to "the Israelites," the Sabbath belongs to Israel, not to the Church.

notes.meaning: The reason for the Sabbath is God's own example. He made the heavens and the earth in six days and rested on the seventh. He rested from creating, not from caring for and ruling his world. Saying God was "refreshed" uses human words to help us understand. Keeping this rest honored God as Creator and pointed to the day his people will rest with him.

When God finished speaking, he gave Moses the two stone tablets of the Ten Commandments. The writing was done "by the finger of God," meaning by God's own power, without any human hand. Stone showed that God's law would last. The two tablets taught duty toward God and toward other people. Matthew Henry adds that only God can write his law on our hard hearts, by his Spirit.
